standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, definition spaces-morphisms-definition-scheme-theoretic-support (cited at statement line 2241)
standard_prerequisites.use: It provides the closed immersion $i : Z \to X$ and the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal{G}$ with $i_*\mathcal{G} = \mathcal{F}$, and makes the statement meaningful because a coherent module is of finite type.

standard_prerequisites.name: A closed immersion is locally of finite type, and a space locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian space is locally Noetherian
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, labels spaces-morphisms-lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type and spaces-morphisms-lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian (invoked at proof lines 2251 and 2252)
standard_prerequisites.use: They show that the scheme theoretic support $Z$ is itself locally Noetherian, which is the hypothesis under which coherence of $\mathcal{G}$ can be tested.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coherence on a locally Noetherian space equals finite type
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-coherent-Noetherian (invoked at proof line 2255)
standard_prerequisites.use: Since $\mathcal{G}$ is of finite type, this gives that it is coherent.

core_obligations: Note that the statement makes sense because a coherent module is in particular of finite type (proof lines 2247-2248).
Show that $Z$ is locally Noetherian: a closed immersion is locally of finite type, and a space locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian space is locally Noetherian (proof lines 2248-2252).
Conclude that the finite type module $\mathcal{G}$ on $Z$ is coherent by the criterion for coherence on locally Noetherian spaces (proof lines 2253-2255).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the quasi-coherent module cut out on the scheme theoretic support of a coherent sheaf by the pushforward identification remains coherent (statement lines 2234-2244). The proof checks that the support is locally Noetherian, using that a closed immersion is locally of finite type, and then applies the characterization of coherence by finite type on a locally Noetherian space. The bookkeeping of the two hypotheses (locally Noetherian support, finite type module) is the substance, so the claim is H2.
